correctness.rationale: The proof uses the standard affine toric divisor sequence and an explicit lattice computation. For a lower facet, the n rays become \(w_q=2\mathbf 1-e_q\); their differences generate the sum-zero root lattice and each has sum \(2n-1\), so the ray-lattice quotient is exactly \(\mathbf Z/(2n-1)\). For an upper facet with \(n\ge3\), ray differences generate the same root lattice while every ray has sum \(-2\), so the ray-lattice quotient is exactly \(\mathbf Z/2\); the free rank is \(n(n-1)-n=n(n-2)\). For \(n=2\), the upper-ray matrix has Smith form \(\operatorname{diag}(1,8)\). The embedded checker independently replays all facet counts and finite lattice identities for \(2\le n\le8\).

value.rationale: The Liu--Zhu varieties are recent extremal examples in the study of alpha invariants, and their singularity structure matters when comparing toric \(\mathbf Q\)-Fano constructions with smoother or Q-factorial regimes. The result gives a complete natural invariant at every torus fixed point: one orbit has cyclic class group of order \(2n-1\), while the other develops free class-group rank \(n(n-2)\) for \(n\ge3\). This quantitatively identifies how non-Q-factoriality grows with dimension and separates the two fixed-point orbits beyond a binary singular/smooth or Q-factorial/non-Q-factorial label.
